subject: Environment
description: Sea level rise, glacier retreat, ocean acidification, IPCC AR6, El Niño / La Niña

questions.stem: The MAJOR cause of recent sea-level rise globally is:

options.option_text: Thermal expansion of seawater + melting of land-based ice (glaciers, Greenland, Antarctic)

questions.explanation: Two main drivers — (1) THERMAL EXPANSION (warmer water occupies more volume; ~40-50% historical contribution); (2) MELTING land-based ice (glaciers + Greenland + Antarctica; growing share post-1990). Sea ice melting (Arctic) does NOT raise sea level (already floating, displacing equivalent volume per Archimedes). Current rate ~3.6 mm/year, accelerating. Total since 1900: ~21-24 cm. IPCC AR6 SSP5-8.5 worst case: ~1.0 m by 2100. Bangladesh, Maldives, Sundarbans — most vulnerable.
questions.subject: Environment

questions.stem: 'Ocean acidification' refers to the ocean becoming more:

options.option_text: Acidic — CO₂ dissolves in water → H₂CO₃ → H⁺ + HCO₃⁻; ocean pH dropping

questions.explanation: Atmospheric CO₂ → dissolves in oceans → forms carbonic acid → releases H⁺ → lowers pH. Pre-industrial pH ~8.2 → current ~8.05 (a 30% increase in [H⁺] since pH is logarithmic). Threatens calcifying organisms — coral, shellfish, plankton — whose shells dissolve in lower-pH water. 'Other CO₂ problem' alongside warming. Ocean has absorbed ~30% of human CO₂ emissions, slowing atmospheric warming but accelerating acidification. Saturation states (Ω) for aragonite + calcite track this.

questions.stem: The IPCC (Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change) was established in 1988 by:
questions.explanation: IPCC — established 1988 by WMO + UNEP. Headquartered in Geneva. Three working groups + Task Force on Greenhouse Gas Inventories. Produces Assessment Reports (AR1 1990, AR6 2021-23) summarising peer-reviewed climate science for policymakers. Doesn't conduct original research. Awarded Nobel Peace Prize 2007 (jointly with Al Gore). Current chair (2023-) — Jim Skea (UK). India represented by Ministry of Environment, IITM Pune.
questions.subject: Environment

options.option_text: Warm-water phase of ENSO — abnormal warming of central + eastern equatorial Pacific that disrupts global weather

questions.explanation: ENSO (El Niño-Southern Oscillation) has two phases. EL NIÑO ('the boy child' — Spanish, named by Peruvian fishermen who first noted it around Christmas) — Pacific trade winds weaken; warm water sloshes east; severe rainfall in S America, drought in Indonesia, Australia, India (often deficient monsoon). LA NIÑA (girl child) — opposite, intensified trade winds, cool central Pacific, often strong Indian monsoon. Cycle every 2-7 years. Modulated by climate change (debated whether becoming more frequent / extreme).

questions.stem: The 'Greenhouse Gas Protocol' classifies emissions into three scopes. Scope-3 emissions are:

options.option_text: All other indirect emissions across the value chain — supplier upstream + customer downstream
Indirect emissions from purchased electricity only

questions.explanation: GHG Protocol scopes — Scope 1: direct emissions (own boilers, vehicles, factories). Scope 2: indirect from purchased energy (electricity, heat, cooling). Scope 3: ALL OTHER indirect — purchased goods, business travel, employee commuting, USE of sold products, waste, distribution, investments. Scope 3 is often largest (~70-90% of corporate footprint) but hardest to measure. SEBI now mandates ESG disclosures for top-1000 listed Indian companies (BRSR — Business Responsibility & Sustainability Reporting from FY 2022-23).
questions.subject: Environment

questions.stem: The current concentration of methane (CH₄) in the atmosphere — over 2.5× pre-industrial — is approximately:
questions.explanation: CH₄ — second largest GHG contributor (~16-20% of warming). Sources: livestock (enteric fermentation), rice paddies, oil/gas leaks, landfills, wetlands, permafrost thaw. Atmospheric lifetime ~12 years (vs CO₂'s centuries) BUT 80× CO₂'s GWP over 20 years. Global Methane Pledge (COP-26 Glasgow 2021) aims 30% cut by 2030 — India NOT a signatory (livestock + paddy concerns). India's CH₄ emissions ~14% of global (mostly enteric fermentation from cattle).
questions.subject: Environment

questions.stem: The largest ice mass on Earth, currently losing >150 Gt/year of ice, is:

options.option_text: Antarctic Ice Sheet (~91% of global land ice; if fully melted, sea level would rise ~58 m)

questions.explanation: Antarctic Ice Sheet — ~26.5 million km³ ice (~91% of global ice; sea-level equivalent ~58 m if all melted). Greenland — ~2.85 million km³ (sea-level equivalent ~7.4 m). Together they hold ~99% of global freshwater ice. Currently losing — Antarctic ~150 Gt/yr (mostly West Antarctica + Antarctic Peninsula); Greenland ~270 Gt/yr accelerating. Himalayan glaciers — much smaller in volume but critical for Asian rivers (Ganga, Indus, Brahmaputra source); 'Third Pole'. ISRO's BHUVAN platform tracks Indian glaciers.
